rule: Admissibility is per seed and unanimous: all three seeds must clear JevBench (cc >= 0.5187 and exact McNemar not significantly worse). One seed failing means the arm is not promoted, whatever the other two do. JevBench is the veto; a seed that regresses on the acceptance set is a real regression, not noise to average away.
Promotion requires a positive held-out delta in all three seeds AND exact McNemar significance in at least two of three. Per-seed deltas and the spread are reported whether or not it clears.

Two of three significant with the third positive promotes. Two of three significant with the third negative does not promote and is reported as unstable. Three positive with one significant does not promote.

No pooled test across seeds. The three seeds are scored on the same 6,254 held-out items, so their per-item results are correlated; concatenating them would treat 6,254 correlated observations as 18,762 independent ones and inflate significance by roughly sqrt(3). A pooled number, if ever wanted, needs a seed-as-random-effect treatment, not a concatenated contingency table.

role: defines the statuses a gate can emit; not the register's whole status field
scope: gate outcomes only. The register also carries lifecycle and artifact labels - registered, running, stopped, note, measured, confirmed, verified, done, blocked and others - which are outside this definition.

definitions.promoted: the arm met the success rule.
definitions.killed: a pre-registered clause closed the arm. Whether the arm completed its seed plan is recorded in the row's own reason; do not infer it from the status. The base-conditioned arm was stopped before its plan; the two scan boundary rows were closed after completing theirs.
definitions.inconclusive: the gate's third branch applies and was not executed; not a verdict.
definitions.not_promoted: the arm ran and missed the success rule.
definitions.control: a role label for a cell that reproduced the control, not a gate verdict. It is defined here because a reproduction cell may need a word; no row in this file currently carries it.

note: `killed` covers two situations - the clause stopped an arm early, and the clause closed an arm that had finished - and the status alone does not distinguish them; the row's reason does. The field is wider than these five: at the time of writing it carries 31 distinct values across 126 rows, plus one row with no status, and the one-offs are sentences rather than states (correction, correction-2, control-measured, control-recheck, measured-ambiguous, diagnostic-mechanism, restarted-bucketed, gate-plan, provenance-note, deviation, not_promoted_admissibility). Mapping the field onto a small set is a separate migration; this note defines only what a gate emits and does not renormalise anything.

applies_to: fresh runs only; never to a result already gated
rule: The point non-regression clause is replaced by the three-state interval screen on JevBench chance-corrected accuracy, with delta = 8 pp. Material regression supported: the 95% upper bound is below -8 pp. Coarse safety screen passed: the 95% lower bound is above -8 pp. Unresolved: the interval crosses -8 pp. A point estimate below -8 pp is not a material regression on its own.

The interval is the normal approximation on the per-item chance-corrected differences at alpha 0.05, and the exact two-sided McNemar p is reported beside it. Both come from model.evaluation.gate.paired_screen, which uses model.scripts.paired_mcnemar for the exact test and model.evaluation.paired_power.detectable_delta for the detectable difference.
8 pp is the instrument's resolution at 231 items, not a scientific tolerance: a genuine 6 pp regression passes the screen. Passing is recorded as 'coarse safety screen passed', never 'non-inferior'.
JevBench remains a veto only on a supported material regression. Effect size stays on the held-out instrument, and no instrument is averaged with another.
The comparison reads the control's exact chance-corrected accuracy at gate time and never a rounded constant.
